dialogues.speaker: Quiauhquetzal
dialogues.text: Staying in high places allows me to sense the scent of danger sooner... Sorry. It's a bad habit from the past.

dialogues.speaker: Quiauhquetzal
dialogues.text: I'm braiding ropes. When I walked on the ground, ropes were our songs.

dialogues.speaker: Quiauhquetzal
dialogues.text: The children whose births I did not witness told me that Great{RUBY#[D]Tribal} Houses of the North taught them how to weave "woven scrolls."

dialogues.speaker: Quiauhquetzal
dialogues.text: But those fabrics were too bulky. If their Great{RUBY#[D]Tribal} Houses were attacked by others...

dialogues.speaker: Quiauhquetzal
dialogues.text: Or burned by the great{RUBY#[S]Sovereign ruler} ruler above our heads, those fabrics couldn't be hidden away as quickly as a rope.

dialogues.speaker: Quiauhquetzal
dialogues.text: Since I can walk {RUBY#[D]live} forever — unlike that brutal man who abducted me — I must sing. I must carve these stories down. Vindia says this is a good thing.

dialogues.speaker: Quiauhquetzal
dialogues.text: Here, it's high up, and you can see far and wide. It's a good place to hide.

dialogues.speaker: Quiauhquetzal
dialogues.text: In our Cal{RUBY#[D]Tribe}pul, being on the ground is considered dangerous. Even if the Great {RUBY#[S]Sovereign Lords} Rulers above us don't decide to wipe us out on a whim, the other Calp{RUBY#[D]Tribes}ulli will still come to plunder us.

dialogues.speaker: Quiauhquetzal
dialogues.text: Perching on the cliffs and in the trees like the quetzals allows us to flee calamity before it strikes.

dialogues.speaker: Quiauhquetzal
dialogues.text: There are no noble beastlords here, nor conquerors who enjoy flaying skin. It's safe, but... I'm used to securing an escape.

dialogues.speaker: Quiauhquetzal
dialogues.text: Goodbye. May you be spared the fearful sight of the great ruler.

dialogues.speaker: Quiauhquetzal
dialogues.text: Ah, Cuauheztli, that savage man who claimed to be the successor of Chaac. He slaughtered everyone in my Great{RUBY#[D]Tribal} House, yet he let me live to serve as his concubine.

dialogues.speaker: Quiauhquetzal
dialogues.text: He believed that as long as he mastered the Phlogiston, he could end the era of the great{RUBY#[S]Sovereign ruler} ruler above our heads. But in the eyes of the great rulers, he was nothing more than an infant wielding a rusted knife.

dialogues.speaker: Quiauhquetzal
dialogues.text: The Great Lord Ix Roq'ratik'obala'{RUBY#[S]"Murmuring Spring"} Ka'alahun Ch'ule-L did not even deign to appear in person. She merely granted me the power of vengeance, so that I might repay blood with blood.

dialogues.speaker: Quiauhquetzal
dialogues.text: And so, I did. Pinning that man beneath the water... It took far less effort than I had initially thought.
